newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says Gulf drugs leader faces new charges.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says Gulf drugs leader faces new charges.

text.p: Mexican authorities said on Thursday that Gulf drug cartel leader Oscar Malherbe de Leon, who was arrested last week, would face new charges after revealing one of his pseudonyms.

Oscar Malherbe de Leon, who took over leadership of the Gulf or Matamoros cartel following the arrest of his boss Juan Garcia Abrego in January last year, had told investigators he also went by the name of Martin Becerra Mireles.

"Against this alias ... an arrest warrant exists ... for the crimes of possession and purchase of marijuana and providing resources for the transportation of the drug," the Attorney General's Office said in a statement.
Malherbe already faces murder, arms and cocaine-trafficking charges.
Malherbe was arrested on Feb. 26 in Mexico City, just as U.S. President Bill Clinton was weighing whether to "certify" for another year that Mexico is an ally in Washington's war on drugs.

As Mexico was announcing his arrest, fellow Gulf cartel capo Humberto Garcia Abrego -- Juan's brother -- mysteriously slipped out of police custody, where he was being questioned in a money-laundering probe.
Mexico withheld news of his escape until after Clinton had announced his decision last Friday to "recertify" Mexico.
U.S. Congressmen from both the Democrat and Republican parties, concerned at high-level drug corruption in Mexico, have sought to overturn Clinton's decision.
They face an uphill battle because such a resolution, if vetoed by Clinton, would need a two-thirds majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives to pass.
